title: Semilinear conormal complex maps and their difference homotopy
statement: Let $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $\alpha:A\to A'$ and $\beta:B\to B'$ be a commutative square of commutative rings. Let $Q\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $T\twoheadrightarrow B'$ be surjective algebra maps over $A$ and $A'$ respectively, and put $I=\ker(Q\to B)$, $J=\ker(T\to B')$. Using Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], form the two-term cochain complexes $N(Q)=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta_Q}\Omega^1_{Q/A}\otimes_QB]$ and $N(T)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta_T}\Omega^1_{T/A'}\otimes_TB']$ in degrees $-1,0$, with $\delta([h])=\mathrm dh\otimes1$. Every $A$-algebra map $a:Q\to T$ inducing $\beta$ on the quotients defines a $\beta$-semilinear chain map $N(a)$ by $[h]\mapsto[a(h)]$ and $\mathrm dx\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(a(x))\otimes\beta(b)$. These induced chain maps preserve identities and composition. For any two such maps $a_0,a_1$ there is a $\beta$-semilinear map $H:\Omega^1_{Q/A}\otimes_QB\to J/J^2$ given by $H(\mathrm dx\otimes b)=\beta(b)[a_0(x)-a_1(x)]$, and it satisfies $N(a_0)^{-1}-N(a_1)^{-1}=H\delta_Q$ and $N(a_0)^0-N(a_1)^0=\delta_TH$. Thus the two chain maps are homotopic. Here semilinear means $H(bm)=\beta(b)H(m)$, or equivalently linear after restricting the target scalars to $B$. Neither $Q$ nor $T$ is required to be polynomial.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause: encode the two surjections by Extension.ofSurjective (Extension/Basic.lean:102). Cotangent.map and map_mk (Extension/Basic.lean:465,482) give the conormal map; CotangentSpace.map_tmul (Extension/Cotangent/Basic.lean:158) gives the differential map; CotangentSpace.map_comp_cotangentComplex (line 205) gives the chain identity; Hom.sub and Hom.sub_tmul (lines 252,285) give H and its formula; Cotangent.map_sub_map and CotangentSpace.map_sub_map (lines 311,290) give the two homotopy identities. Identities and composition are Cotangent.map_id/map_comp (Extension/Basic.lean:488,498) and CotangentSpace.map_id/map_comp (Extension/Cotangent/Basic.lean:173,176). All maps are already linear over the restricted source scalars; no polynomial hypothesis occurs. Read all these lines; no comparison with a full derived cotangent complex is needed.
